Between specific intermediate stages the gas is dehydrated and achieves pipeline quality water content. 4 PIPELINE DESIGN DATA 4.1 DESIGN PRESSURE System MOP of 2,500 psig will be considered in all pipeline stress calculations. 4.2 DESIGN TEMPERATURE Maximum and minimum design temperatures for pipeline system are in accordance with Table 4-1 Table 4-1 Design Temperature Pipeline Maximum Design Temperature 120OF Below Ground Pipeline Minimum Design -20OF Temperature Above Ground Pipeline Minimum Design -50OF Temperature Pipeline Operating Temperature 105OF 77 OF, Summer Pipeline Installation Temperature 40 OF, Winter Page 8 of 20 Design Basis Memorandum 1997-000-PL-DBM-0001 Revision: 0 Pipeline Scope - FEED Date: April 28, 2023 4.3 DESIGN FACTOR The default design factor for mainline, line pipe shall be 0.72. All road crossings and fabricated assemblies (mainline valves and launchers/receivers) piping shall be designed with a 0.6 design factor. Major HDDs (Highways/rivers/etc.) in populated areas and railroad crossings shall be designed with a 0.5 design factor. 5 PIPELINE SYSTEM DESCRIPTION 5.1 ALIGNMENT Pipeline Alignment Sheets used for construction illustrate criteria consistent with requirements by Pipeline Hazardous Material Safety Administration (PHMSA), the U.S Army Corp of Engineers (USACE) and other permit agencies, showing centerline, construction workspace, access roads and environmental features, such as wetlands and streams. FEED will not have Alignment Sheets, but will have route maps at a larger scale with less information. Construction alignment sheets will be generated during detail design for the contractor bid packages and subsequently for the packages for construction. As‐built alignment sheets will be generated during the installation phase, showing the final location of the pipeline and the installed materials. 5.2 RIGHT‐OF‐WAY A 40‐ft permanent easement will be considered as a default for the proposed pipeline diameters. An additional 70-foot of temporary workspace (TWS) is planned for conventional upland lay. However, it may be adjusted for environmental features, other construction factors, regulatory agency restrictions, and landowner demands. Additional workspace will be provided at foreign pipeline crossings, road, railroads, topsoil segregation, wetland, waterbody crossings, and wherever needed to facilitate construction activities. Additional workspace needed for pipe string fabrication and drilling/boring activities will be determined based on survey data and ingress / egress to the site. 6 PIPELINE DESIGN 6.1 PIPELINE MATERIALS 6.1.1 Pipe Specification The pipe for the OES Project will be fabricated according to API 5L Specification, Latest edition and manufactured in accordance with Project Specifications.
